A1.justification: Both PDFs describe 3DScenePrompt with the same authors, framework and retained experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 includes a readable appendix with sections A–F.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original video-generation evaluations on RealEstate10K and DynPose-100K, baseline comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds DAVIS evaluations, further ablations, reconstruction-component comparisons, runtime measurements and qualitative outputs in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Appendix A explicitly extends inference through iterative autoregressive generation and introduces a DepthAnything v3 variant replacing MegaSAM at inference. These are limited procedural extensions; the CogVideoX backbone, dual conditioning and three-stage dynamic masking remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds DAVIS evaluation of iterative long-video generation, extending coverage beyond the next-chunk evaluations in v1 to generation with accumulated autoregressive history. RealEstate10K and OpenVid-1M training sources and RealEstate10K/DynPose-100K evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds CameraCtrl with latent interpolation and CameraCtrl with FreeLong as evaluated long-video comparators. Existing main-table comparator sets remain unchanged. CameraCtrl2, APT2 and SPMem receive new discussion but are not added as experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include autoregressive DAVIS evaluation with RMSE, MSE and ATE reporting; temporal-window and zero-spatial-conditioning controls; masking-stage experiments on a DynPose-100K subset; and component/runtime comparisons. Appendix B also changes the stated static-training reconstruction tool from MegaSAM to VGGT. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 tests masking on/off and spatial-frame counts. v2 retains these and adds cumulative masking-stage ablations, temporal windows w=1/5/9, an n=0 spatial-prompt control, and reconstruction-component and runtime analyses in Tables 6–10. These directly examine previously untested component roles and practical costs.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Additional result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 3 and 4 and existing Table 2 scores are retained. v2 adds the w=1 result, Tables 5–10 and qualitative outputs: examples include DAVIS PSNR 17.28 for the proposed method and DynPose-100K PSNR 13.4534 for its DepthAnything v3 variant versus 13.0468 with MegaSAM. These are new experiments or variants, not improvements to retained same-setting results. Table 7 also reports w=9 VBench values differing from unchanged Table 3 without explaining the discrepancy.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the conditional-latent definition from concatenating separately encoded conditions to encoding their concatenation. This changes the displayed mathematical composition, although v1 Figure 3 already depicts a shared encoder and an implementation change is not established. The core numbered equations remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: static 3D scene memory and dual spatio-temporal conditioning enable camera-controlled continuations from arbitrary-length context while preserving scene consistency and motion. Revised wording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations separating spatial prompts' camera-control role from temporal context's motion-continuity role, explains soft geometric guidance versus inpainting, and discusses replaceable reconstruction components. Appendices A and D introduce substantive limitations concerning autoregressive error accumulation, reconstruction overhead and dependence on mask quality.

D1.justification: v2 specifies approximately 30K RealEstate10K and 20K OpenVid-1M training videos, filtering criteria, geometry tools, SEA-RAFT usage, 49-frame chunk accounting and component-level runtimes. Appendix E adds a future code-release commitment. However, v1 Section 3.5's explicit last-T-frame target and preceding-context construction is omitted; existing optimizer, hardware and training-budget details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds multi-frame conditioning work, including CameraCtrl2 and Seaweed-APT2. Appendix C substantially expands positioning against persistent embodied world models, WorldMem, SPMem and video inpainting. References for new experiments and tools are added, while several earlier supporting citations, including RAFT and Direct2V, are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introductory/method paragraphs are rewritten, related-work headings are refined, and the main-text training-data section is replaced by a shorter appendix account. A notation guide and appendices organize the additions, while most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds six experimental tables, a notation table and five figures, including qualitative comparison grids and long-video timelines. Table 2 gains a conditioning variant. Existing figures are retained with resizing, label/caption adjustments and reflow; the substantial change is the expanded visual evidence and display structure.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important evidential gap in v1 by adding a zero-spatial-prompt control, temporal-window comparisons and stage-wise masking tests, substantially improving attribution of the framework's benefits. Long-video evaluation, runtime breakdowns, curation details and explicit limitations also improve practical assessability. These gains outweigh the omitted target/context construction details and reporting weaknesses: Tables 3 and 7 contain unreconciled VBench values, and the latency discussion overstates comparability with CameraCtrl and MotionCtrl relative to Table 10.
